newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki sags but seen joining European rally.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki sags but seen joining European rally.

text.p: Shares sagged in mixed trade on Thursday but came off lows in late dealings as Nokia turned to a higher close, and brokers expected Helsinki to catch up with a European rally on Friday.

Weaker-than-expected U.S. retail sales data eased fears of a near-term interest rate rise and sent the Dow climbing nearly one percent to 7643.21 points, and also boosted European stocks further in the late afternoon.
"The figures were good, and Europe was strong, I see no reason why we should not follow," one broker said.

Nokia was in focus -- closing up 0.50 markka at 364.00 after it shrugged off a report that Goldman Sachs had cut its Intel 1997 EPS estimate -- but UPM-Kymmene was also lively. YIT was third liveliest with Merita crossing 900,000 shares in-house at 67.00 markka.

Investment company Norvestia said after trade had ended that it was interested in bidding for part of Amer's controlling K shares and to take a main owner position together with some current K shareholder. Amer has been weak recently on doubts about the intentions of Jonathan Bryan Guinness, who plans to take control of the group by buying K shares.
